evidence: 7 atomic/source voices contribute the 50 positives; all material is synthetic/TTS or derived. The split report identifies 9 atomic voice IDs overall and speaker overlap across every split.
interpretation: Real human speaker diversity is not present; TTS voice count is not equivalent to speaker diversity.

evidence: Positive TTS metadata explicitly covers pitch offsets [-2.0, 0.0, 2.0] semitone-like units, but only for synthetic voices and only 50 positive clips.
interpretation: Coverage is a designed TTS grid, not natural pitch variation.

evidence: Positive TTS metadata explicitly covers speed factors [0.85, 1.0, 1.15]; confusable negatives also have measured speed values.
interpretation: Natural rate variability is absent because the dataset is synthetic/derived.

evidence: No level, RMS, LUFS, peak, SNR, or gain metadata exists in the manifest.
interpretation: Cannot establish measured level coverage without waveform analysis.

evidence: No microphone, device, codec, channel, or frequency-response metadata exists; all clips are 48 kHz.
interpretation: Device diversity cannot be established from the manifest.

evidence: No room, enclosure, acoustic treatment, or room-ID metadata exists; no RIR source is represented in the manifest.
interpretation: No evidence of real-room acoustic diversity.

evidence: No reverberation/RIR metadata or RIR source is represented.
interpretation: RIR augmentation can cover some synthetic room variation, but cannot replace real recordings.

evidence: There are 1000 standalone synthetic noise clips across white, pink, hum, fan, and click sources, but no manifest category represents speech+noise mixtures.
interpretation: Noise type diversity exists, but deployment SNR/mixture diversity is absent.

evidence: Fan and clicks are represented; white/pink noise and hum are also present.
interpretation: Real household/office/vehicle/outdoor soundscapes are not represented.

evidence: The manifest has no clipping, codec, bit-depth, channel-count, SNR, or quality metrics; all files are reported at 48 kHz.
interpretation: Waveform inspection is required before enabling quality-specific transforms.

evidence: No distance, source-to-microphone distance, SPL, geometry, or near/far label exists.
interpretation: Cannot infer distance from duration, speaker, or filename.

evidence: 1199 phonetic/lexical confusables plus 800 positive-derived partial-wakeword negatives are present.
interpretation: These are the most deployment-relevant negative sources currently represented, but they are still predominantly synthetic/derived.

evidence: The manifest sources are TTS, synthetic noise, or positive-derived truncations; no real microphone-recorded source is identified.
interpretation: This is the principal limitation for deployment realism.
